1	# wal-store
2	
3	Key value store that appends every mutation to a write-ahead log first, so a process killed between writes and checkpoints recovers exactly the committed state.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m wal_store --path ./store recover
16	    python3 -m wal_store --path ./store put <key> --value-file <path>
17	    python3 -m wal_store --path ./store get <key>
18	
19	## Public interface
20	
21	`wal_store.Store(path)` opens the store directory. The directory must
22	exist; opening a missing path raises `FileNotFoundError` (the `put` command
23	line subcommand creates it).
24	- `put(key, value) -> None` records a mutation.
25	- `get(key) -> bytes | None` reads the current value.
26	- `delete(key) -> None` records a removal.
27	- `delete_range(start=None, end=None) -> None` records a batch removal of
28	  every committed key in a half-open byte range (`delete(start, end)` is
29	  the same call).
30	- `commit() -> int` advances the durable sequence number.
31	- `recover() -> dict` replays the log and reports what it applied.
32	- `compact() -> dict` rewrites committed history into one tight log and
33	  reclaims the old space, without changing the committed state or the
34	  durable sequence.
35	- `scan(start=None, end=None) -> ScanCursor` opens an ordered read-only
36	  cursor over the committed snapshot pinned at that moment.
37	- `stats() -> dict` reports sequence, entries and bytes.
38	
39	## Scanning
40	
41	`scan()` works on both open forms and never touches the write path. The
42	returned cursor is an iterator of `(key, value)` pairs in bytewise key
43	order — keys compare by their raw UTF-8 bytes and values come back as the
44	exact stored bytes, with no encoding conversion — covering `start`
45	inclusive through `end` exclusive; a `None` endpoint leaves that side
46	unbounded, so `scan()` walks everything. Keys that only ever appeared in
47	delete records never show up, a key overwritten any number of times yields
48	only its last committed value, and empty values scan like any other. A
49	writer's uncommitted changes are not part of the snapshot; a read-only
50	store scans the snapshot it pinned at open.
51	
52	The snapshot is materialised once when the cursor opens, so later commits,
53	compaction, crash recovery and reclamation of the old log space never
54	change what the cursor yields, and the same snapshot scans to the identical
55	sequence before and after compaction. Scanning never replays the log,
56	takes no lock and keeps no history in memory, so its cost is independent
57	of the log's length. A `start` that sorts after `end` raises `ValueError`,
58	as does reading from a cursor after `close()` (the cursor is also a
59	context manager).
60	
61	## Range deletes
62	
63	`delete_range(start=None, end=None)` removes every committed key a scan
64	of the same endpoints would return: keys compare by their raw UTF-8
65	bytes, the range is half-open (`start` inclusive, `end` exclusive) and a
66	`None` endpoint leaves that side unbounded, so `delete_range()` clears
67	the whole store while `delete_range("a", "a")` removes nothing. The
68	shorthand `delete(start, end)` is the same call; `delete(key)` still
69	removes one key. Endpoint validation is shared with `scan`: non-string
70	endpoints raise `TypeError` and a `start` sorting after `end` raises
71	`ValueError`.
72	
73	Like every other mutation the tombstone is only staged in the session:
74	it is invisible to scans and read-only stores until `commit()`, and a
75	writer that is killed first reopens at the last committed state. Once
76	committed, the covered keys disappear from single-key reads and scans
77	alike, and a key that only ever appears in delete history can never come
78	back. Writing a key inside a previously deleted range simply stores the
79	new value — after commit it reads back as that last committed value,
80	with keys and values still handled as raw bytes.
81	
82	Recovery resolves a range tombstone by removing the covered keys; the
83	report counts the tombstone record under `applied`. Compaction reclaims
84	it together with the rest of the dead history: the compacted image
85	contains one live put per surviving key and no tombstones at all, so
86	reclaiming the record can never resurrect a deleted key, and a snapshot
87	scans to the identical bytes before and after compaction.
88	
89	## Read-only stores
90	
91	`wal_store.Store(path, read_only=True)` opens an isolated reader. Any
92	number of read-only processes may coexist with the single writer in the
93	same directory. A reader takes no lock and never creates or changes a
94	file; it pins a snapshot at open time and every `get` reads from that one
95	complete committed snapshot, so uncommitted mutations, a half-written
96	commit, a torn record or a half-finished shrink are never visible.
97	Successive reads from the same reader may advance across snapshots only by
98	reopening; each read is of one fully committed snapshot. Reads do not
99	replay the log and do not block the writer: killing or suspending a reader
100	never affects the writer's commits, recovery or stats. `put`, `delete`,
101	`commit` and `recover` are rejected on a read-only store; `stats` reports
102	the pinned snapshot and `get` is the normal way to read it. Readers serve
103	from the atomically replaced `wal.ckp` sidecar (and the committed log
104	prefix), so directories written by older versions open directly.
105	
106	`wal_store.inject_tear(source, destination, offset)` is a verification aid:
107	it writes a byte-for-byte copy of `source` cut at exactly `offset` bytes (a
108	replica of a process killed at that write position) to `destination` and
109	leaves the source untouched. Either argument may be a store directory, in
110	which case its `wal.log` is used. A negative or past-the-end offset raises
111	`IndexError`. It is never used by the normal write path.
112	
113	## Recovery
114	
115	`recover()` returns a report with three integer fields, in this key order:
116	
117	- `applied` — committed put/delete records replayed into the state,
118	- `discarded` — torn tail records dropped (at most one, the unfinished final
119	  write left by a process killed mid append; `0` on a clean log),
120	- `seq` — the durable sequence number after recovery.
121	
122	A record killed halfway through is not a mutation: it is discarded and the
123	recovered state is exactly the last committed state. An empty log recovers
124	to an empty state, which is a normal result. Recovery truncates the dirty
125	tail and the next commit uses `seq + 1`, no matter how often the store is
126	reopened.
127	
128	### Recovery may itself be killed
129	
130	Recovery is an idempotent, kill-safe convergence. Interrupting it at any
131	point — while the dirty tail is being dropped or the log is being rebuilt —
132	and reopening any number of times reaches exactly the state and the report
133	of one clean recovery, with exit code `0`; the durable sequence never
134	regresses and the next commit is always `seq + 1`.
135	
136	Two internal sidecar files in the store directory make this work; they are
137	not part of the public API and are maintained entirely below the write
138	path:
139	
140	- `wal.ckp` is an atomically replaced copy of the log prefix ending at the
141	  most recent commit marker. A log torn at *any* offset — even offset 0, or
142	  inside the committed prefix — is silently rebuilt from it, so a
143	  half-finished convergence can never be mistaken for a torn tail or for
144	  corruption.
145	- `wal.rec` is a small marker written after validation and before the
146	  repair, recording the clean prefix length and the discarded count. A
147	  repair interrupted mid-copy is simply repeated on reopen, and the marker
148	  keeps `discarded` stable across reopens and repeated recoveries until the
149	  next successful commit closes the epoch.
150	
151	Only the final record may be incomplete. Any incomplete record elsewhere,
152	a length out of bounds, unparseable content, or a duplicate/regressing
153	sequence is corruption: recovery raises `wal_store.CorruptLogError`
154	(a subclass of `ValueError`) and stops without applying or removing
155	anything.
156	
157	The command line `recover` prints the report as one compact JSON line with
158	the same key order and a trailing newline, e.g.
159	`{"applied":2,"discarded":0,"seq":1}`. Discarding a torn tail is not an
160	error and the exit code is `0`; corruption prints one explanatory line to
161	standard error and exits `3` without printing the JSON line.
162	
163	## Compaction
164	
165	`compact()` reclaims history without sacrificing any committed state. When
166	it finishes, the log contains exactly the live committed key/values: one
167	put frame per currently committed key, in sorted key order, followed by a
168	base commit marker that carries the pre-compaction sequence. Deleted keys
169	are gone for good — a deleted key can never reappear — and overwritten keys
170	keep only their final value. The durable sequence number is unchanged, so
171	the next `commit()` writes `seq + 1` and subsequent commits continue the
172	strict sequence as if no rewrite had happened. The empty committed state
173	(including "everything was deleted") compacts to an empty log.
174	
175	`compact()` returns the same three-field report shape as `recover()`:
176	`applied` is the number of live puts the new log contains, `discarded` is
177	always `0` and `seq` is the preserved sequence. Uncommitted session changes
178	make it raise `ValueError`; commit or discard them first.
179	
180	Compaction is a kill-safe, idempotent convergence like recovery. The new
181	image is assembled in memory and durably staged as the `wal.cmp` sidecar
182	(an atomically replaced complete file, never an in-place edit), then
183	published in two atomic steps — `wal.ckp` first and `wal.log` second —
184	before the staging file is removed. A process killed at any point, any
185	number of times, leaves a store that finishes the identical publish on the
186	next open: the recovered state is exactly the last committed state, the
187	sequence never regresses and the resulting log/sidecar bytes are
188	byte-identical to one uninterrupted compaction. Repeating compaction on an
189	already compact store produces the same bytes.
190	
191	Live read-only stores are unaffected: they keep serving the complete
192	snapshot they pinned before, during and after compaction (it lands on the
193	other half of the same log-versus-checkpoint pair readers already choose
194	between), while fresh readers open the compacted snapshot. No reader ever
195	sees a mix of old and new bytes, a half-written file, or content whose
196	space was reclaimed; killing a reader does not disturb compaction and
197	killing the compactor does not disturb a reader. Compaction introduces no
198	new limits beyond the existing single-writer rule, and directories written
199	by older versions compact directly with no conversion step.
200	
201	## Tests
202	
203	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
204	
205	## Limits
206	
207	One writer at a time; no cross-process locking.
208	Values are bytes; encoding is the caller concern.
209	No replication; compaction is a writer-initiated rewrite, not background
210	garbage collection.

The command line `recover` prints the report as one compact JSON line with
the same key order and a trailing newline, e.g.
`{"applied":2,"discarded":0,"seq":1}`. Discarding a torn tail is not an
error and the exit code is `0`; corruption prints one explanatory line to
standard error and exits `3` without printing the JSON line.

## Compaction

`compact()` reclaims history without sacrificing any committed state. When
it finishes, the log contains exactly the live committed key/values: one
put frame per currently committed key, in sorted key order, followed by a
base commit marker that carries the pre-compaction sequence. Deleted keys
are gone for good — a deleted key can never reappear — and overwritten keys
keep only their final value. The durable sequence number is unchanged, so
the next `commit()` writes `seq + 1` and subsequent commits continue the
strict sequence as if no rewrite had happened. The empty committed state
(including "everything was deleted") compacts to an empty log.

`compact()` returns the same three-field report shape as `recover()`:
`applied` is the number of live puts the new log contains, `discarded` is
always `0` and `seq` is the preserved sequence. Uncommitted session changes
make it raise `ValueError`; commit or discard them first.

Compaction is a kill-safe, idempotent convergence like recovery. The new
image is assembled in memory and durably staged as the `wal.cmp` sidecar
(an atomically replaced complete file, never an in-place edit), then
published in two atomic steps — `wal.ckp` first and `wal.log` second —
before the staging file is removed. A process killed at any point, any
number of times, leaves a store that finishes the identical publish on the
next open: the recovered state is exactly the last committed state, the
sequence never regresses and the resulting log/sidecar bytes are
byte-identical to one uninterrupted compaction. Repeating compaction on an
already compact store produces the same bytes.

Live read-only stores are unaffected: they keep serving the complete
snapshot they pinned before, during and after compaction (it lands on the
other half of the same log-versus-checkpoint pair readers already choose
between), while fresh readers open the compacted snapshot. No reader ever
sees a mix of old and new bytes, a half-written file, or content whose
space was reclaimed; killing a reader does not disturb compaction and
killing the compactor does not disturb a reader. Compaction introduces no
new limits beyond the existing single-writer rule, and directories written
by older versions compact directly with no conversion step.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

One writer at a time; no cross-process locking.
Values are bytes; encoding is the caller concern.
No replication; compaction is a writer-initiated rewrite, not background
garbage collection.

282	def _iter_frames(f):
283	    """Scan an open binary log file from position 0.
284	
285	    For every intact frame yields
286	    ``("frame", meta, value, start, end)``. Scanning stops with either no
287	    terminal event (clean EOF), ``("torn", start)`` for a single incomplete
288	    final frame, or ``("invalid", start)`` for a frame that fails framing,
289	    header/payload checksum or metadata parsing. With the header checksum a
290	    partial header that borrows bytes from a following record cannot survive,
291	    so a short read landing exactly at EOF is reliably the one unfinished
292	    record a single writer was appending when it died; bytes left beyond such
293	    a read instead make it corruption.
294	    """
295	    f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
296	    eof = f.tell()
297	    f.seek(0)
298	    while True:
299	        start = f.tell()
300	        header = f.read(_HEADER)
301	        if not header:
302	            return
303	        if len(header) < _HEADER:
304	            # Trailing bytes of a frame header are a torn tail only when
305	            # nothing follows them; a gap anywhere else is corruption.
306	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
307	                   else ("invalid", start))
308	            return
309	        if header[:4] != _MAGIC:
310	            yield "invalid", start
311	            return
312	        if int.from_bytes(header[_PREFIX:], "big") != zlib.crc32(
313	                header[:_PREFIX]):
314	            yield "invalid", start
315	            return
316	        length = int.from_bytes(header[4:_PREFIX], "big")
317	        if length > _MAX_PAYLOAD:
318	            yield "invalid", start
319	            return
320	        payload = f.read(length)
321	        checksum = f.read(_TRAILER)
322	        if len(payload) < length or len(checksum) < _TRAILER:
323	            # Only the single final record may be incomplete.
324	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
325	                   else ("invalid", start))
326	            return
327	        if int.from_bytes(checksum, "big") != zlib.crc32(payload):
328	            yield "invalid", start
329	            return
330	        newline = payload.find(b"\n")
331	        if newline < 0:
332	            yield "invalid", start
333	            return
334	        try:
335	            meta = json.loads(payload[:newline])
336	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
337	            yield "invalid", start
338	            return
339	        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not isinstance(meta.get("t"), str):
340	            yield "invalid", start
341	            return
342	        yield "frame", meta, payload[newline + 1:], start, f.tell()

513	    @staticmethod
514	    def _validate(frames, terminal):
515	        """Validate every frame and the strictly increasing commit sequence.
516	
517	        Returns ``(committed_end, last_seq)`` -- the byte offset just past
518	        the last commit marker and its sequence number. An ``"invalid"``
519	        terminal is corruption and raises ``CorruptLogError``; a ``"torn"``
520	        terminal is left for the caller, which decides from the durable
521	        checkpoint whether it is a tail to discard or a gash to restore.
522	
523	        A compacted image starts with a base commit marker (``"b"``) that
524	        carries the pre-compaction sequence: it must be the first commit
525	        marker in the file, it establishes the expected sequence at
526	        ``seq + 1`` and no second base marker may ever follow. An ordinary
527	        first commit must still be sequence 1.
528	        """
529	        expected_seq = 1
530	        last_seq = 0
531	        committed_end = 0
532	        for meta, _value, _start, end in frames:
533	            op = meta.get("t")
534	            if op in (_OP_PUT, _OP_DELETE):
535	                key = meta.get("k")
536	                if not isinstance(key, str) or key == "":
537	                    raise CorruptLogError(
538	                        f"invalid frame metadata: {meta!r}")
539	            elif op == _OP_RANGE:
540	                # Both endpoints must be present and be a string or null;
541	                # the bounds must not be reversed.
542	                lo, hi = _range_bounds_from_meta(meta)
543	                if lo is not None and hi is not None and lo > hi:
544	                    raise CorruptLogError(
545	                        f"range tombstone endpoints out of order: {meta!r}")
546	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
547	                seq = meta.get("s")
548	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
549	                    raise CorruptLogError(
550	                        f"invalid base commit marker: {meta!r}")
551	                if last_seq != 0:
552	                    raise CorruptLogError(
553	                        "base commit must be the first commit marker")
554	                if seq < 1:
555	                    raise CorruptLogError(
556	                        f"base commit sequence {seq} out of order")
557	                last_seq = seq
558	                expected_seq = seq + 1
559	                committed_end = end
560	            elif op == _OP_COMMIT:
561	                seq = meta.get("s")
562	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
563	                    raise CorruptLogError(
564	                        f"invalid commit marker: {meta!r}")
565	                if seq != expected_seq:
566	                    raise CorruptLogError(
567	                        f"commit sequence {seq} out of order, "
568	                        f"expected {expected_seq}")
569	                last_seq = seq
570	                expected_seq += 1
571	                committed_end = end
572	            else:
573	                raise CorruptLogError(f"unknown frame type: {op!r}")
574	        if terminal is not None and terminal[0] == "invalid":
575	            raise CorruptLogError("corrupt log frame")
576	        return committed_end, last_seq

578	    @staticmethod
579	    def _replay(frames) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], int]:
580	        state: dict[str, bytes] = {}
581	        applied = 0
582	        for meta, value, _start, _end in frames:
583	            op = meta["t"]
584	            if op in _COMMIT_OPS:
585	                continue
586	            if op == _OP_PUT:
587	                state[meta["k"]] = value
588	            elif op == _OP_RANGE:
589	                lo, hi = _range_bounds_from_meta(meta)
590	                for key in [k for k in state
591	                            if _key_in_range(k.encode("utf-8"), lo, hi)]:
592	                    del state[key]
593	            else:  # _OP_DELETE
594	                state.pop(meta["k"], None)

607	    @staticmethod
608	    def _copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, length: int) -> None:
609	        remaining = length

611	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
612	            if not chunk:

704	    def _rebuild_log(self, clean_end: int) -> None:
705	        """Make the log exactly its clean ``[0, clean_end)`` prefix.
706	
707	        Kill-safe and idempotent: when a checkpoint covers the prefix the new
708	        log is fully written and fsynced as a temp file and atomically renamed
709	        over the old one, so a kill leaves either the old log or the complete
710	        restored log -- never a half-written file -- and rerunning converges.
711	        Without a checkpoint but with the committed bytes still at stable
712	        offsets, a synced truncate drops the tail instead. The empty prefix is
713	        a truncate to zero.
714	        """
715	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
716	        if size == clean_end:
717	            return
718	
719	        if clean_end == 0:
720	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
721	            os.fsync(self._fd)
722	            return
723	
724	        try:
725	            ckp_size = os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path)
726	        except FileNotFoundError:
727	            ckp_size = -1
728	
729	        if ckp_size < clean_end and size > clean_end:
730	            # No checkpoint, but the committed bytes survive at stable
731	            # offsets: drop the dirty tail. Idempotent if killed mid-call.
732	            try:
733	                os.fsync(self._fd)
734	            except OSError:
735	                pass
736	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, clean_end)
737	            os.fsync(self._fd)
738	            return
739	        if ckp_size < clean_end:
740	            raise CorruptLogError(
741	                "committed prefix is torn and no checkpoint covers it")
742	
743	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
744	        with open(self._ckp_path, "rb") as fsrc, open(tmp, "wb") as fdst:
745	            self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, clean_end)
746	            os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
747	        # Windows cannot rename over a path held open by the append fd.
748	        os.close(self._fd)
749	        try:
750	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
751	            _fsync_dir(self._dir)
752	        finally:
753	            self._fd = os.open(
754	                self._path,
755	                os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY, 0o644)

757	            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")

761	    def _build_compact_image(self, seq: int) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
762	        """Serialise the committed state into one compact log image.
763	
764	        One put frame per live key, keys in sorted order, followed by a base
765	        commit marker carrying the pre-compaction sequence. The empty state
766	        at seq 0 is an empty image rather than a zero-sequence marker.
767	        """
768	        if seq == 0:
769	            return b"", 0
770	        parts = [_encode_frame(_OP_PUT, value, key=key)
771	                 for key, value in sorted(self._data.items())]
772	        parts.append(_encode_frame(_OP_BASE, seq=seq))
773	        return b"".join(parts), len(self._data)

775	    def _read_compact_candidate(self):
776	        """Validate ``wal.cmp`` as one compacted image.
777	
778	        Returns ``(image, end, seq, live)`` where ``image`` is the exact
779	        byte content, or ``None`` when the sidecar is absent. The image must
780	        be a clean file ending exactly on a base commit marker, preceded only
781	        by put frames with strictly increasing keys; anything else is
782	        corruption of the crash-convergence machinery, never a discardable
783	        tail (the sidecar is always atomically replaced, never written in
784	        place).
785	        """
786	        try:
787	            f = open(self._cmp_path, "rb")
788	        except FileNotFoundError:
789	            return None
790	        with f:
791	            image = f.read()
792	        if not image:
793	            # An empty candidate encodes the empty state at seq 0.
794	            return b"", 0, 0, 0
795	
796	        frames, terminal = self._scan_bytes(image)
797	        if terminal is not None:
798	            raise CorruptLogError(
799	                "compaction candidate is not a clean committed prefix")
800	        end, seq = self._validate(frames, None)
801	        if end != len(image) or seq <= 0:
802	            raise CorruptLogError(
803	                "compaction candidate has bytes past its base commit")
804	        live = 0
805	        last_key: str | None = None
806	        saw_base = False
807	        for meta, _value, _start, _end in frames:
808	            op = meta.get("t")
809	            if op == _OP_PUT:
810	                if saw_base:
811	                    raise CorruptLogError(
812	                        "compaction candidate has puts past its base commit")
813	                key = meta["k"]
814	                if last_key is not None and key <= last_key:
815	                    raise CorruptLogError(
816	                        "compaction candidate keys are not sorted uniquely")
817	                last_key = key
818	                live += 1
819	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
820	                if saw_base:
821	                    raise CorruptLogError(
822	                        "compaction candidate has multiple base commits")
823	                saw_base = True
824	            else:
825	                raise CorruptLogError(
826	                    "compaction candidate contains a non-compacted frame")
827	        if not saw_base:
828	            raise CorruptLogError(
829	                "compaction candidate ends without a base commit")
830	        return image, end, seq, live

833	        """Frame-scan raw bytes as if they were a log file."""

837	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
838	                if event[0] == "frame":
839	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
840	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
841	                else:

845	    def _install_log_bytes(self, image: bytes) -> None:
846	        """Atomically replace the log with ``image`` and reopen the fd.
847	
848	        The complete image is written and fsynced as a temp file first, so a
849	        kill leaves either the old log or the complete new one -- never a
850	        half-written log. The append fd is closed for the rename because
851	        Windows cannot replace a path held open by it, then reopened.
852	        """

860	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)

864	                self._path,
865	                os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY, 0o644)

869	    def _install_compaction(self, image: bytes, seq: int) -> None:
870	        """Publish a staged compacted image; idempotent and kill-safe.
871	
872	        The torn-tail marker is dropped first: its byte offset belongs to
873	        the old (longer) log and must not outlive the shrink. Checkpoint is
874	        replaced next and the log last, both via complete-file atomic
875	        renames, then the candidate is removed. Any ordering of a kill
876	        between those steps leaves the durable files equal to either the old
877	        pair or the complete new pair, and rerunning (via the surviving
878	        candidate) converges to the same compacted bytes.
879	        """
880	        # Compaction closes any prior recovery epoch the way a commit does;
881	        # do it while the old log still exists so a later kill replays this
882	        # whole publish from the durable candidate.
883	        self._remove_marker()
884	
885	        if seq == 0:
886	            # Empty committed state: the log is zero length and there is no
887	            # checkpoint to publish; reclaim every old byte and drop the plan.
888	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
889	            os.fsync(self._fd)
890	            try:
891	                os.unlink(self._ckp_path)
892	                _fsync_dir(self._dir)
893	            except FileNotFoundError:
894	                pass
895	            self._remove_candidate()
896	            return
897	
898	        def write(fdst):
899	            fdst.write(image)
900	
901	        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)
902	        self._install_log_bytes(image)
903	        self._remove_candidate()

912	    def _finish_compaction(self) -> None:

914	
915	        With a single writer a present candidate means its compaction never
916	        finished (no later commit was possible), so the log and checkpoint
917	        cannot be ahead of it; the publish is simply repeated. A candidate
918	        whose boundary a newer durable epoch has overtaken is stale and is
919	        discarded instead.
920	        """
921	        candidate = self._read_compact_candidate()
922	        if candidate is None:
923	            return
924	        image, _end, cand_seq, _live = candidate
925	
926	        log_seq = 0
927	        if os.path.exists(self._path):
928	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._path)
929	            _log_end, log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
930	        ckp_seq = 0
931	        ckp = self._read_clean_prefix(self._ckp_path)
932	        if ckp is not None:
933	            _frames, _end, ckp_seq = ckp

940	    def _converge(self):
941	        """Validate and converge the on-disk log to its clean state.
942	
943	        Returns ``(frames, discarded)`` for the now-clean log. Raises
944	        ``CorruptLogError`` without changing anything if the log is corrupt.
945	        Safe to run repeatedly and safe to kill at any point.
946	
947	        The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log
948	        boundary, the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can
949	        never regress. A log torn inside its committed prefix is rebuilt from
950	        the checkpoint and ``discarded`` stays 0 (those bytes were committed,
951	        not an unfinished write); a torn or merely uncommitted tail past the
952	        boundary is discarded, and the marker freezes that report until the
953	        next commit even when the kill lands mid-repair.
954	        """
955	        self._remove_stale_temps()
956	        # A durable compaction candidate left by a killed compact() is
957	        # published before ordinary convergence; it is itself a complete
958	        # committed prefix, so this never invents or loses a committed byte.
959	        self._finish_compaction()
960	        marker = self._read_marker()
961	        marker_end = -1
962	        marker_discarded = 0
963	        if marker is not None:
964	            marker_end, marker_discarded = marker
965	
966	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
967	        log_end, _log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
968	        ckp_end = self._checkpoint_boundary()
969	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
970	
971	        target = max(log_end, ckp_end, marker_end)
972	        # The target bytes must come from somewhere still on disk: the
973	        # validated log itself or the checkpoint.
974	        if target > log_end and target > ckp_end:
975	            raise CorruptLogError("recovery target has no durable source")
976	
977	        log_clean = terminal is None and size == log_end
978	
979	        if log_clean and log_end == target:
980	            # Nothing to repair. An old marker whose epoch a newer commit
981	            # closed durably can finally go; otherwise its discarded count
982	            # stays frozen until that commit.
983	            if marker is not None:
984	                if target > marker_end:
985	                    self._remove_marker()
986	                    discarded = 0
987	                else:
988	                    discarded = marker_discarded
989	            else:
990	                discarded = 0
991	            if ckp_end < target:
992	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
993	            return frames, discarded
994	
995	        if target > log_end:
996	            # Committed bytes were torn away (offset 0 included): the
997	            # checkpoint is the source of truth. The discarded count is only
998	            # meaningful when the marker pins this exact boundary.
999	            discarded = marker_discarded if target == marker_end else 0
1000	            self._rebuild_log(target)
1001	        else:
1002	            # A dirty suffix sits past the boundary. Decide discarded from
1003	            # the suffix itself: a torn final record counts, complete
1004	            # uncommitted frames do not. This also covers a repair killed
1005	            # before the rebuild (the original suffix is still here, so the
1006	            # same decision is reached) and fresh writes appended after a
1007	            # previous repair (a new crash is a new decision rather than the
1008	            # old marker's). A marker is only frozen once the log itself is
1009	            # rebuilt clean; see the clean branch above.
1010	            discarded = 1 if terminal is not None else 0
1011	            if ckp_end < target:
1012	                # Make the prefix independently restorable before we publish
1013	                # the plan or remove any bytes.
1014	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
1015	            self._write_marker(target, discarded)
1016	            self._rebuild_log(target)
1017	
1018	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
1019	        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
1020	        if end != target or terminal is not None:
1021	            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")
1022	        return frames, discarded

1045	    def _open_read_only(self) -> None:
1046	        """Pin a committed snapshot without creating or modifying anything.

1048	        No lock is taken and nothing on disk is written. The reader chooses
1049	        the highest committed prefix available at the instant it opens --
1050	        the validated prefix of ``wal.log`` or the existing ``wal.ckp``
1051	        sidecar, which the writer replaces atomically as part of every
1052	        commit -- scans that prefix once into memory, and serves every
1053	        ``get`` from that index. Later reads are independent of log history,
1054	        never replay the log and never block the writer.
1055	
1056	        The checkpoint is a complete, self-contained image that is never
1057	        modified in place (only atomically replaced), so reading it cannot
1058	        expose uncommitted bytes, a half-written commit, a torn record or a
1059	        half-finished rebuild/shrink. It is also what makes the pin safe once
1060	        the reader closes the file: the image survives any later rename.

1062	        frames, end, seq = self._choose_readonly_prefix()
1063	        state, _applied = self._replay(frames)
1064	        self._ro_index: dict[str, bytes] = state
1065	        self._ro_seq = seq
1066	        self._ro_entries = len(frames)

1069	    def _choose_readonly_prefix(self):

1074	        merely uncommitted tail past the last commit is excluded; a framing
1075	        or sequence failure in committed bytes is corruption and raises
1076	        ``CorruptLogError``. The checkpoint is the source when a crash or a
1077	        concurrent rebuild has torn/shrunk the committed log bytes.
1078	        """
1079	        log_frames = None
1080	        log_end = -1
1081	        log_seq = 0
1082	        if os.path.exists(self._path):
1083	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._path)
1084	            log_end, log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
1085	            # Keep only frames at or before the last commit; the torn final
1086	            # record already arrives as the terminal, not as a frame.
1087	            log_frames = [fr for fr in frames if fr[3] <= log_end]
